title: Chapter 30
content:
Heavy storm clouds bruised the night sky, pregnant with rain, while a brisk, cool wind rustled through the surrounding woods.

Jakyeong stared down at the spread of drinks and appetizers the staff had set on the low patio table. The glass of sweet, peach-scented cocktail clearly belonged to him, while the crystal tumbler of cask-strength whiskey was for Kang Il-hyun.

Plucking an ice cube from the bucket, Jakyeong rolled the cold cube across his palm, gazing out over the pool. Submerged LED fixtures slowly cycled through ambient tones, shifting the water from deep sapphire to rich emerald. From the outdoor speakers, low, mellow jazz drifted into the night.

He tossed the ice cube into the pool, watching the ripples distort the underwater lights. Amused by the simple motion, he flicked a few more cubes into the water before pushing himself up from the lounger. Dipping a hand into the basin, the water was surprisingly cold. He shook the droplets from his fingers and paced the flagstone deck.

After returning from the funeral and having dinner, Il-hyun had insisted on spending the evening by the poolside. Jakyeong had flatly refused, but the man had simply ignored the protest. With the target flash drive already located in the penthouse safe, Jakyeong had zero tactical reason to linger around the mark. Yet knowing that further refusal would only provoke another round of psychological harassment, he had reluctantly come outside to put in an appearance.

Sinking onto the sun lounger, Jakyeong took a testing sip of the cocktail. It tasted far more like artisanal juice than alcohol—too sugary for his personal palate, but pleasant enough. Draining half the glass, he picked up a delicate canapé from the platter. The staff had proudly informed him that the garnish was top-tier Beluga caviar, dusted with flecks of edible gold leaf.

As he chewed the savory bite, a persistent mosquito landed on his forearm. He brought his palm down sharply, crushing the pest. A bright smear of blood stained his skin—it had already fed on someone else. Scowling, he wiped the mess on a napkin. The grounds had undergone pest control just days ago, but being completely enveloped by dense forest meant moths and biting insects were an inescapable hazard.

"Not going in for a swim?"

A man wrapped in a charcoal-gray bathrobe stepped onto the deck. For a second, Jakyeong failed to recognize him.

Fresh from the shower, Il-hyun’s damp dark hair was combed entirely forward, falling softly over his brow. It was the first time Jakyeong had seen him without his signature slicked-back executive style. The casual fringe took years off his sharp features, making him look remarkably youthful—though still undeniably a mature man in his early thirties.

"How is the drink? The mixologist crafted it specially for tonight."

Il-hyun had hired a private bartender for the evening, promising the man could concoct whatever drink they desired. Since Jakyeong's alcohol tolerance capped out at two or three glasses, the effort felt wildly excessive.

As Jakyeong took another sip, Il-hyun turned his back, untied the belt, and slipped the heavy robe off his broad shoulders.

Picking a maraschino cherry from his drink, Jakyeong’s eyes locked onto the expanse of Il-hyun's bare back. The man’s physique was irritatingly flawless. Dense, sculpted muscle wrapped tight over a broad frame without a single ounce of excess fat, proportioned with athletic precision.

The lack of large-scale ink was rather unexpected; Jakyeong had half-expected an underworld boss of his pedigree to carry a sprawling dragon across his shoulder blades.

Jakyeong popped the cherry into his mouth just as Il-hyun turned around.

The breath caught in Jakyeong's throat. He nearly choked on the cherry pit.

Did this bastard stuff a pair of rolled socks down the front of his briefs, or what?

Striding forward with effortless confidence, Il-hyun picked up his whiskey glass. "Cheers."

Standing bare inches from the edge of the sun lounger, the prominent, heavy contour pressing against the fabric of his swim briefs was impossible to ignore. Whether the man was semi-aroused or simply built like a thoroughbred was an open question. Fighting to keep a neutral expression, Jakyeong instinctively leaned his torso back against the cushions.

"Care for another?"

Startled, Jakyeong looked up to find Il-hyun offering a fresh cocktail cherry skewered on a silver pick.

"You seemed to enjoy the first one."

Phrasing, you absolute menace.

Jakyeong shook his head firmly. He wished the man would either dive into the pool or sit down on a lounger instead of hovering over him half-naked. Turning away felt like admitting defeat, but staying locked in place was deeply grating.

"Why do you keep stealing glances at my groin?"

Jakyeong felt a vein twitch in his temple. He looked up, meeting Il-hyun’s smug, amused grin.

"I wasn't staring... You're the one thrusting it directly into my line of sight."

"An optical illusion, surely. When you're packing this much, it tends to draw the eye even when you're standing perfectly still."

"..."

Lying in bed last night, Jakyeong had briefly found himself contemplating Kang Il-hyun’s miserable life—losing his mother as a child, only to have his own father order a contract hit on his head in adulthood. He had felt a fleeting, microscopic pang of pity.

Yet the moment this man opened his arrogant mouth, every shred of sympathy evaporated into thin air. He truly deserves everything coming to him.

Jakyeong turned his head away, pointedly ignoring him. Il-hyun set his glass on the table and stepped into the water. The gentle splash of the pool blended harmoniously with the steady chirping of crickets in the brush.

Watching from the lounger, the pool lights caught the sharp ridges of Il-hyun's back as water cascaded over his skin. With his hair down, he looked like a completely different person.

Il-hyun pushed off the wall and submerged. He cut through the water in a single, fluid underwater glide, navigating the entire length of the pool with the effortless grace of an aquatic predator. His boast about athletic prowess hadn't been an exaggeration. Reaching the opposite basin, he executed a clean flip-turn against the tile, gliding all the way back to the shallow end before breaking the surface.

He burst through the water, sweeping his wet hair back from his forehead as he offered Jakyeong a broad, radiant smile.

Jakyeong sat motionless, momentarily captivated despite himself. The bastard is infuriatingly handsome.Catching himself staring, he snapped his focus away toward the tree line.

Il-hyun climbed out of the water, snatched his bathrobe, and pulled it over his shoulders. Tying the belt tight, he gritted his teeth with a sharp hiss.

"Fuck me. That is freezing."

Jakyeong barely swallowed a sudden burst of laughter, clamping a hand over his mouth to avoid spraying his drink. Look at him. After swaggering into the water like an unstoppable force of nature, he was shivering like a normal human. It was oddly grounding.

Seeing Jakyeong struggle to keep a straight face, Il-hyun crossed the flagstones and dropped into the lounger directly opposite him.

"Find that amusing?"

Jakyeong cleared his throat and shook his head, but the laughter refused to die. He rarely laughed out loud, but the sheer absurdity of the moment cracked his defenses. His cheeks twitched from the strain of suppressing his grin, forcing him to bury his face between his knees to hide the amusement.

"Look at that."

Jakyeong slowly lifted his head from his knees.

"That's the first time you've ever genuinely smiled."

The observation hit Jakyeong like a physical strike.

Il-hyun picked up his drink, gazing silently across the rippling surface of the pool. With both of them quiet, the hum of insects in the forest grew pronounced.

A waiter stepped onto the deck, discreetly swapping Jakyeong's empty glass for a fresh cocktail. The liquid was deep indigo and layered with swirling silver luster, looking like a miniature galaxy suspended in crystal. Intrigued, Jakyeong gently swirled the stemware.

"Do you ever miss your mother?"

The question sounded like something posed to a homesick child. Caught off guard, Jakyeong shook his head.

"We speak on the phone regularly, so... I'm fine."

"What does it feel like?"

"Pardon?"

"Having a mother."

Jakyeong fell silent. What did it feel like?

"It's... nice."

He had no idea what was driving Il-hyun’s sudden melancholy. He knew the bare facts of how Il-hyun’s mother had died—hanging herself from the second-floor balcony years ago. Why had she done it? Did even the matriarch of an untouchable criminal dynasty suffer beneath the surface? The rhythmic hum of the forest suddenly sounded terribly bleak.

Staring blankly at the still water, Il-hyun spoke in a quiet, measured cadence.

"Whenever I look at a swimming pool, I think of my late mother."

It was the first time Il-hyun had ever volunteered a detail about his past.

"Did... did you swim together when you were little?"

"No. She tried to drown me in one."

"..."

"And not long after that, she hanged herself."

"..."

Il-hyun drained the whiskey in one swallow, his brow tightening into a pained knot before turning his dark eyes back toward Jakyeong.

"I don't blame her. Forced to live with a man she despised, only to give birth to a monster like me... it must have been unbearable."

Jakyeong sat frozen, words failing him entirely.

Il-hyun let out a heavy, dragging sigh, tilting his chin toward the overcast sky. "Ah... I miss my mother."

What is his angle now? The sudden plunge into tragic melodrama left Jakyeong thoroughly unsettled. As he cautiously gauged the man's expression, Il-hyun slowly turned his head, fixing him with a heavy, intense gaze.

"I wish someone would comfort me."

There wasn't a single drop of genuine grief in those pitch-black pupils.

"Comfort me, Yi-an."

Putting on a mournful, kicked-dog expression that looked utterly ridiculous on a hardened killer, Il-hyun extended an open hand. It wasn't pathetic—it was deeply unnerving.

Jakyeong picked up a slice of watermelon from the fruit platter, giving his head a firm, unyielding shake. When it came to parents trying to murder their own offspring, Jakyeong had a library of gruesome memories that could easily trump Il-hyun's pool story.

"Comfort," Il-hyun repeated, dragging out the syllables.

Ignoring the bizarre plea, Jakyeong turned his back, quietly nibbling on his watermelon.

Meanwhile, the local mosquito population was treating him like an all-you-can-eat buffet. For some infuriating reason, the pests were targeting him exclusively while completely ignoring the man beside him. Even the mosquitoes know you're toxic, don't they?

As Jakyeong swatted at his ankles, Il-hyun placed a fresh cigarette between his lips, rose from the lounger, and extended a hand downward.

"Let's head inside. The bugs are getting out of hand."

Hesitating for a second, Jakyeong took the offered palm. Il-hyun began hauling him upright, but as Jakyeong found his footing, Il-hyun’s grip suddenly wrenched hard to the side.

What—

Jakyeong scrambled for balance, but the momentum was unstoppable.

He was launched clean off the flagstone deck, plunging straight into the freezing pool.

He surfaced with a furious gasp, sputtering water, only to find Kang Il-hyun standing at the edge of the coping, cigarette smoke curling around a thoroughly wicked, villainous grin.

"What the hell was that for?!" Jakyeong shouted, wiping water from his eyes.

"You should have comforted me when you had the chance."

Holding his whiskey glass in one hand, Il-hyun took a casual step backward, giving a mocking little wave. "Stay in there and reflect on what you did wrong. You're not allowed out until you're genuinely sorry."

With that, the man spun on his heel and strolled casually toward the house.

Floating in the freezing basin, Jakyeong realized his horn-rimmed glasses were gone. Scanning the illuminated water, he spotted the black frames drifting lazily beside a half-eaten wedge of watermelon.

God damn it.

He retrieved the glasses and hauled himself up onto the stone deck, shivering as the cold night air bit into his soaked clothes. Grinding his teeth in absolute fury, he took two steps toward the villa—just as heavy, fat raindrops began to pelt down from the dark sky.

Jakyeong looked up at the weeping clouds, his eyes burning with pure, unadulterated venom.
